extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and news reporters covering politics, elections, and labor disputes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for news reporters on covering political stories (especially elections and forecasts) and labor troubles/strikes, including what to include, how to treat bias, and opportunities for human-interest and constructive reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of election stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Three common kinds of election stories are: (1) an analysis of political conditions preceding an election with or without a forecast of the result, (2) a description of election day conditions and events, (3) the results of the election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elections require a different handling than ordinary political news; choose the appropriate type (analysis/forecast, day-of description, or results) and tailor reporting accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present both sides fairly; confine partisanship to editorials
rubrics_metrics.description: Although some newspapers are sufficiently independent in politics to treat political news without partisan bias, many papers still present such news from the point of view of their editorial policy. There is a growing tendency, however, to present both sides fairly in news columns and to confine partisanship to editorials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News copy should aim for fairness and balanced presentation of opposing viewpoints; overt partisanship belongs in opinion/editorial pages rather than news columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election returns — essential content elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Election return stories consist largely of summaries of the most important results of the election, such as: (1) the candidates elected and defeated, (2) the majority or plurality of the successful candidates, (3) the effect of the election on the political complexion of legislative bodies, (4) causes of victory and defeat, (5) statements by candidates and party managers in regard to the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these specific items when summarizing results so readers understand who won, by how much, the legislative consequences, root causes, and reactions from actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political forecast / analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: An analysis of political conditions preceding an election with or without a forecast of the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground forecasts in reporting: canvass local areas, use check lists and registration figures, compare to previous votes, account for defections and local issues (e.g., prohibition), and cite knowledgeable local party workers and leaders when estimating likely outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election-day reporting — conditions, turnout, incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of election day conditions and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report weather, ballot/design effects, voting speed and turnout statistics (percent by times of day), administrative logistics (inspectors, deputies, sample ballots, instruction), notable incidents or disputes at polling places, human anecdotes (individual voters, volunteers/watchers), and any irregularities or enforcement actions; use specific times, percentages, and eyewitness detail to convey the day's flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and accurate presentation in labor stories
rubrics_metrics.description: A fair and accurate presentation of the points of view of both the employers and the employees is essential in all stories of this kind. Statements from both sides, therefore, are important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always seek and include statements from employers and workers/unions; avoid one-sided accounts and ensure factual accuracy when reporting claims, offers, and denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of human-interest treatment in labor coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Although stories in this class are largely informative, there is also a chance for human interest treatment. Accounts of living and working conditions, for example, as obtained from workmen and their families often give a better picture of the circumstances that produced the strike than do formal statements by labor leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement factual reporting with on-the-ground human details — living conditions, family impact, personal anecdotes — to explain causes and make the story relatable; these often illuminate underlying issues better than formal statements alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate creation of sympathy when warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: Sympathy may be legitimately created for the strikers and their families, especially when they are in actual want or are plainly the victims of oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists may portray sympathetic elements (e.g., material hardship) when supported by evidence; do so responsibly, making clear the factual basis for eliciting reader sympathy rather than editorializing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive journalism — furnish all facts for intelligent understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the settlement of labor troubles not infrequently is brought about by the influence of public opinion, constructive journalism recognizes the importance of furnishing readers with all of the facts necessary for an intelligent understanding of the issues and conditions involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be comprehensive and explanatory: provide context, history, economic and social facts, demands and offers, arbitration possibilities, and consequences so readers can form an informed judgment; avoid withholding material that is necessary for understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report negotiation specifics and demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the concrete demands, employer offers, proposals for arbitration, and the specific points in dispute (wage scale percentages, representation rights after promotion, seniority or promotion authority, hours and overtime arrangements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When covering labor negotiations include the precise issues at stake, proposed terms (percentages, hours, pay arrangements), positions of both sides, any arbitration proposals, duration of negotiations, and whether sympathetic strikes or broader tie-ups are likely — these details explain stakes and prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report scope, impact, and human consequences of strikes
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the scale of the dispute (number of workers involved, mileage or systems affected), likely or actual economic impact (tie-ups, closures), occurrence of sympathetic strikes, and any violence or casualties resulting from clashes (including militia involvement, ammunition, deaths, and appeals for aid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual, measured accounts of scope and consequences: numbers, geography, timelines, casualty counts, rescue and relief actions, and international/consular appeals where relevant; such detail conveys the seriousness and broader repercussions of labor troubles.
